What is this app (contents): I believe that trust is essential. I believe that trust is built on experience. This app helps people build trust by providing a reliable way to set up postponed bonus payments
What is shorter (contents): The app is for escrows. Transparent, reliable, reputation-building escrows. Mainly, for setting up not regular payments but bonus payments. E.g., as projects come to an end, any contractor starts to look for the next job. Putting money on the table motivates them
The idea (contents): Yep, but... no dispute resolution. There is little sense in using on-chain contracts while still relying on human intervention in case of disputes. So, there is no third party. Only a funder, a grantee, and the contract. Everybody knows all the possible outcomes from the beginning. It is rigid, and thus predictable
Balance is key (contents): The absence of judges means all the power balancing is written in the contract. The funder cannot get their money back at any time. The grantee can lose money if their relationship with the giver deteriorates
The details (contents): 1. The funder sets up a sum and a date when the grantee can claim it. 2. For the first quarter of the period, the funder can revoke the whole amount; for the second quarter — only half; for the third — only one third; and for the last quarter — only one quarter. 3. Once the date arrives, if there is money (i.e., if the funder has not revoked the escrow right away), the grantee can claim the sum. 4. But if the grantee does not do so for 30 days, the funder can take the whole sum back
How can I trust you (contents): Don't trust me, trust the code! <1>GitHub<1> <2>Etherscanner<2> You can play with it on the Sepolia test network. Just change the net in the top bar
Why does it leave some money in the allo: Why does it leave a non-zero allowance?
It leaves the smallest amount to lower transaction fees the next time you fund an escrow. This is how it works: going from 1 to any value is much cheaper than going from 0 to that value
Approve allowance tip: In case of transaction error your money must stay yours, so instead of transfering in advance you allow the contract to transfer it on your behalf alongside the escrow creation. So, if something goes wrong, nothing is spent, you can just set the allowance to 0 and be safe
